edges.cite: OWASP XSS Prevention / HTML Sanitization guidance
edges.note: A sanitizer rebuilds markup keeping only an allowlist of safe elements/attributes: positive validation applied to HTML.

edges.cite: OWASP Input Validation Cheat Sheet (canonicalize before validate)
edges.note: Input must be reduced to canonical form first so encoded variants cannot slip past the allowlist match.
Sanitizers must decode/normalize entities and encodings before allowlisting so obfuscated script cannot survive.
Paths/URLs must be canonicalized before the access check, else equivalent encodings bypass mediation (path traversal).
The untainting step that clears tainted data before a sink is typically an allowlist validation.
Taint tracking flags SQL sinks; binding values via a prepared statement is the sanctioned way to consume tainted data.
For XSS sinks the approved untaint step is HTML sanitization of the tainted markup.

edges.cite: OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet (primary + additional defenses)
edges.note: Parameterization is the primary SQLi defense; allowlist validation is the recommended additional layer (defense in depth).
HMAC and keyed-hash MACs are constructed by applying a cryptographic hash to key-mixed message.
Random nonces/IVs must be drawn from a CSPRNG so they are unpredictable and non-repeating.

edges.cite: OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet (salt from CSPRNG)
edges.note: The per-entry salt must be generated by a CSPRNG to defeat precomputation.
Anti-CSRF tokens must be unpredictable, so they are generated by a CSPRNG.

edges.cite: OWASP / NIST crypto guidance on timing-safe tag verification
edges.note: MAC tag verification must use constant-time comparison to avoid leaking the tag via timing.
Comparing derived password hashes should be timing-safe to avoid a side channel on the digest.
CSRF/double-submit token equality checks should be constant-time so timing does not leak the token.
Image measurement hashes the next stage; the signature is verified over that digest before handoff.
A/B update stages an image that verified boot must authenticate before it is booted or rolled back.
The bootloader verifies the next-stage image immediately before performing the jump/handoff.
Symmetric keys and plaintext buffers should be zeroized right after AEAD use to limit memory exposure.
The plaintext password buffer should be scrubbed immediately after the hash is computed.
Entropy pools, seeds and derived key material should be zeroized after use to prevent recovery.
Each Merkle node is the cryptographic hash of its children, giving collision-resistant integrity.
Objects are addressed by the cryptographic hash of their content, giving integrity and dedup.
The monitor consults the object's ACL (a column of the access matrix) to decide each request.
With capability-based protection the monitor validates the presented unforgeable token authorizing the access.
RBAC supplies the authorization rules the monitor evaluates on each mediated access.
Check Point is a concrete, configurable realization of complete-mediation authentication/authorization decisions.

edges.cite: Schumacher et al., Security Patterns (POSA); Yoder & Barcalow
edges.note: Routing all entry through one guarded point makes complete mediation by the monitor tractable.
The monitor records each access decision to the audit log for accountability and later reconstruction.
Check Point logs authentication/authorization violations to the audit trail as it penalizes them.
Audit entries are attributed to the authenticated identity carried by the security session.
Tamper-evident append-only logs chain entries with a cryptographic hash so alteration is detectable.

edges.cite: Yoder & Barcalow, Architectural Patterns for Enabling Application Security (PLoP'97)
edges.note: Both are members of the same pattern language; entry funnels through the access point onto the secure layer.
The secure access layer wraps platform mechanisms the Check Point invokes for its decisions.
A secure database access layer exposes only bound/parameterized statements to callers.
The subset of operations shown is derived from the user's roles/permissions.
Because everything is shown, each unauthorized attempt is rejected at the Check Point at use time.
The session object is created at the single access point once login succeeds and carried thereafter.
The session caches the subject's roles/permissions so each request need not re-derive them.
Session identifiers must be unpredictable, so they are generated by a CSPRNG.
The anti-CSRF token is bound to and validated against the authenticated session.
Checkpoint ordering/cadence is verified by the watchdog manager, which resets on violation.
Control-flow supervision and plausibility checks are complementary independent monitors of correct execution.
Watchdog catches hangs (liveness); sanity check catches implausible outputs (correctness): complementary fault classes.
Both detect a failed/hung component by missed periodic signals; watchdog is local, heartbeat is across a link.
On a missed deadline the watchdog forces the system into a predefined safe state (or reset).
When a plausibility check fails, fault handling drives the system to a safe state.
Every set/get on a smart-data type runs a range/plausibility check on the value.
Smart data can carry a CRC in its metadata and verify it on access to detect silent corruption.
Both harden critical data against memory corruption: smart data via range/CRC metadata, one's-complement via inverted duplicate.
Competing integrity schemes for stored critical data: bit-inverted duplicate vs a computed CRC.

edges.cite: Douglass, Real-Time Design Patterns (Protected Single Channel)
edges.note: The single channel is augmented with CRC integrity checks so corruption is detected without redundant hardware.
One integrity augmentation for the single channel is inverted-duplicate storage of critical variables.
Range/plausibility checks are the monitoring the protected single channel adds at points along the path.
A heterogeneous dual channel is realized with diversely implemented (N-version) channels to catch systematic faults.
On channel disagreement the comparator safes the system by switching to a safe state.
Debug allocators combine poisoned fill of freed memory with guard/redzone pages to catch overruns and use-after-free.
Use-after-free hardening pairs poisoning freed memory with NULLing-and-checking the pointer after free.
Verifying a pointer against an invalid/NULL sentinel before dereference is a plausibility check on pointers.
Validating pointer arguments at an API boundary is part of completely checking all incoming parameters.

edges.cite: Bloch, Effective Java (Item: make defensive copies; Item: minimize mutability)
edges.note: Both stop external aliases mutating internal state; immutability removes the need, else copy defensively.
Both give isolation from shared mutable state; defensive copy is eager, copy-on-write defers the copy until write.
At a trust boundary untrusted mutable input is both validated and defensively copied before it is retained.
